A: real data and minimal data (what each.summary: Most v3 parts are coded carefully against leakage and are honest in their own docs. But on the data a real mid-market shop has (orders, discount codes, sends and clicks; no margin, no views or carts, rupee amounts) and at its size, most of the "smart" parts either never switch on or are quietly reset, and nobody is told. Nothing tells the marketer which parts are actually running. The plan's "honest levels by data size" message does not exist in the code. Some parts are actively harmful with the preset on. The journeys' "never read" rule counts only clicks, so it stops all email to the 67-92% of a list that has not clicked in 5 or more sends, even customers who buy after every email. Every money constant (WhatsApp 0.03, complaint cost 2.0, the "high value" bar of 50, the default order value of 50) is in dollars, but the code reads it in whatever currency the shop uses, so in India WhatsApp is about 25x underpriced. The early-signal model, meant to give 90-day answers in a week, passed its own backtest and still credited about ₹103 per customer to a nudge that, by construction, only moved purchases earlier. The live tests cannot crown a realistic winner. At 8k customers an arm must beat the default by about 135% of the mean profit per customer; at 300k, by about 23%. The honest lift range is 3-10%. Copy elimination needs about 5,000 sends per draft within one customer type, yet an 8k shop gets 300 types of about 27 people. On top of that, the look-alike crowd, the tiredness crowd and the experiment book live only in memory. They are wiped whenever approved content or the budget envelope changes, and v3's own weekly copy and auto-budget do both. The look-alike and profile models never see non-event attributes, so the plan's real-data bar on MegaFon and Criteo cannot be met by design. Experiments, early signals, auto-budget, copy and images are not wired into the runtime at all; the parts that are wired run on defaults the marketer never sees. Verdict through this lens: v3 is a well-tested set of components whose core claims ("learns from look-alikes", "runs its own experiments", "90-day answer in 1-2 weeks") are unproven at target sizes, and in places false on real data.
sound: Point-in-time discipline is real: profile, slow models, look-alike outcomes and early-signal labels all drop post-as_of events and refuse windows that have not closed yet (autonomy/profile/facts.py header, autonomy/decide/lookalike.py:161, autonomy/decide/slow_models.py censoring).
Opens are correctly never treated as engagement, because mail privacy proxies make them unreliable (autonomy/profile/facts.py:23-24).
Shopify discount codes reach offer_id, and voids or cancellations become REFUND events (autonomy/connectors/shopify/mapping.py:138-152, 178-186).

The slow models gate themselves out of time. On a synthetic orders-only shop (2,000 customers, 14 months), risk passed at AUC 0.83 and value at skill 0.14 in 1.4 s. On orders-only data they genuinely work.
Proof rewards are intent-to-treat with a same-cutoff last-touch rule, which avoids the group-dependent window bias (autonomy/proof/rewards.py:20-58).

The experiments use always-valid mSPRT intervals with Bonferroni-split alpha, a pre-registered pick rule and a hard 10% cap. The statistics are conservative and valid; the problem is power, not correctness.
The look-alike model falls back exactly to the prior below its gates, and its per-customer weight cap stopped a false ready=True in the smoke run (docs/v3/LOOKALIKE.md smoke run).
Real-calibrated Gym scenarios (Hillstrom and MegaFon fits on the train half) are a genuine improvement over purely planted truths (autonomy/gym/scenarios.py REAL_EMAIL_FIT and REAL_SMS_FIT).
The docs are unusually candid about what is pending: Gym and real-bench comparisons not run, vision check 100% by construction, experiments not wired.

findings.assumption: The early-signal model can read an experiment or the agent in 1-2 weeks, because it predicts each customer's 90-day margin from first-week behaviour and passes a backtest (plan-v3 decision 8; EARLY_SIGNALS.md).
findings.problem: The model is trained on untreated history: week-1 orders mean high future value there. A message or discount that only pulls a purchase forward creates week-1 orders without creating margin, so early_read credits it with 90-day value it never earns. The backtest checks monthly cohort means, not treatment differences, so it passes anyway. The interval covers only spread between customers, not the model's own error (early_signal.py:563-565).
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Marketing-ai-/b3510c52-036a-5471-a52e-fd5d81ce4bd7/scratchpad/redteam/early_probe.py: 3,000 synthetic customers with heterogeneous order rates and 14 months of history. The agent group's nudge only moves 244 existing future purchases into week 1, so its true extra margin is 0 by construction. Output: `usable: True 1.0` (backtest share within band 100%); `early read agent-holdout forecast 90d margin/customer: (92.9, 38.3, 147.5)`; `same groups, NO nudge: early read diff (-10.1, -62.8, 42.7)`; `=> effect attributed to a nudge that adds exactly 0 margin: 103.0 per customer`. Code: autonomy/learning/early_signal.py:1-50 (features second_order, log_orders, log_week_margin) and 549-565.
findings.real_world_impact: Discount-heavy arms and goals, which are exactly the ones that pull purchases forward and cannibalise, look 'clearly positive' early. Auto-budget and the Analyst (analyst.py:409-441, `_early_section`) would move money to them and tell the marketer so with a confident interval. This repeats v2's 10x value overestimate in a new form.
findings.recommendation: Do not use a surrogate model trained on untreated history to read treatment effects. At most show it as a 'leading indicator' with no money claim. Validate it only on past randomised campaigns (treated against control, surrogate effect against final effect), never on cohort means. Add the pull-forward probe above as a test that must fail loudly.

findings.assumption: Journeys skip a channel only for people who 'never open' it, and 'turning journeys on takes no channel away' (plan-v3 decision 4; journeys.py:26-27).
findings.problem: never_read() treats a channel as unread after 5 lifetime SENDs with zero clicks and zero replies. Purchases do not count; opens are (rightly) ignored; imported Klaviyo send history counts toward the 5. With journeys on, every email journey is withheld from such a customer, and so are their single email bids (journeys.py:424-429: `and not never_read(...)`). Most of a real list has never clicked, so the v3 preset stops emailing most of the list, or pushes those customers to WhatsApp-only journey C where they have WhatsApp consent.
findings.evidence: autonomy/decide/journeys.py:338-349 (clicks/replies only), 413-414, 424-429; configs/v3/journeys.yaml:16 (`never_open_after_sends: 5`); autonomy/data/folder.py:256-275 (sends counts every SEND event, last_engaged_at only on CLICK/REPLY). Probe: `5 emails, 0 clicks, (bought after each) -> never_read: True`. With a list-average 2% click rate (heterogeneous Beta(0.2,9.8)): `after 5 sends ... never-read = 92%`, `after 20 ... 80%`, `after 60 ... 67%`.
findings.real_world_impact: 8k Shopify+Klaviyo shop with 14 months of weekly campaigns: on day 1 of AUTONOMY_V3, roughly two-thirds of the list gets no email from the agent, including buyers who purchase without clicking (they type the URL or use the app). Revenue falls with no alert. Where WhatsApp consent exists, traffic moves to the channel that is about 100x dearer and can get the number banned.
findings.recommendation: Count purchases and site visits after a send as evidence of reading. Do not count imported pre-agent sends, or require far more sends. Never remove single-message bids. Report in the briefing how many customers a channel was dropped for.

findings.assumption: Costs and value bars are 'in the goal's currency', so WhatsApp (about 100x email) goes only where its uplift pays (plan-v3 decision 4).
findings.problem: The runtime never passes per-shop costs: settings.py:380 says 'The agent keeps its own default channel costs'. Every money constant is USD-sized: DEFAULT_CHANNEL_COSTS email 0.001 and WhatsApp 0.03 (bidders.py:150-158), COMPLAINT_COST 2.0 (agent.py:1136-1138), ValueModel.default_order_value 50 (models.py:279), journey value_bar 50 (configs/v3/journeys.yaml:38,44). Brief.currency defaults to 'USD' (goals.py:57). In a rupee shop all of these are read as rupees.
findings.evidence: autonomy/runtime/settings.py:370-395 (factory builds without costs=); autonomy/decide/bidders.py:150-160; autonomy/runtime/agent.py:1136-1138; autonomy/decide/journeys.py:443 compares value_if_converted (AOV x 0.4 margin = 480 for a ₹1,200 AOV) with a bar of 50, so every customer is 'high value'.
findings.real_world_impact: India launch: a WhatsApp marketing message really costs about ₹0.8-0.9 but is priced at ₹0.03. Complaints cost ₹2. WhatsApp-first journeys C and D are open to everyone. The agent overuses WhatsApp, the channel V-1 itself calls irreversible if burned, and reports inflated net profit per send.
findings.recommendation: Make every currency-bearing constant a required per-shop setting with no dollar default, and refuse to start without channel costs. Derive value bars from shop quantiles (for example the top 20% by clv_90d), not absolute numbers.

findings.assumption: The agent keeps getting smarter: the look-alike crowd learns nightly, the Scientist's experiments run for weeks, and the tiredness model learns from look-alikes (foundations B and C, decision 7).
findings.problem: The look-alike rows and OutcomeBook, the LookalikeHazard crowd and the ExperimentBook are in-process memory. A goal's policy is rebuilt whenever its approved content set or its brief envelope changes (service.py:3044-3054; MATERIAL_BRIEF_FIELDS includes envelope, service.py:304-306). The replay does not refill the crowd (LOOKALIKE.md:72-79; FREQUENCY.md:165-166), and resolve_v3 creates a fresh empty ExperimentBook on every build (runtime/v3.py:123). v3's own designs trigger rebuilds: weekly copy gets new content ids per ISO week (COPY.md:48-52), and auto-budget moves arrive as new brief versions (PRESET.md 'Offer pricing and the budget planner').
findings.evidence: autonomy/runtime/service.py:3044-3054; autonomy/runtime/service.py:304-306; autonomy/runtime/v3.py:118-124; docs/v3/LOOKALIKE.md:72-79; docs/v3/PRESET.md 'What the preset does not fix' (experiment book not persisted, crowd starts empty after a restart).
findings.real_world_impact: The marketer approves a new message on Tuesday; the running offer test silently disappears and the look-alike model returns to the plain click model until enough new 7-day windows close. With weekly content changes the crowd may never accumulate more than a week or two of rows. No alert says this happened.
findings.recommendation: Persist the outcome rows, the hazard crowd and the ExperimentBook in the store and rebuild them from the decision log on policy build. Separate 'content changed' from 'rebuild models'. Until then, the preset should refuse to turn on experiments in the runtime.

findings.assumption: The agent runs its own live experiments within 10% of the agent group and keeps winners; it 'learns something every few weeks at 20k+ customers' (DECISIONS V-3).
findings.problem: With always-valid intervals, alpha split over 2k-1 comparisons, min 200 per arm, max_days 28 and a 10% cap, the detectable gain is far above realistic offer differences. On top of that, nothing in the runtime ever starts, reviews or promotes an experiment: only autonomy/experiments/gymrun.py calls book.start, review or promote. The planted Gym truth used to 'prove' it is a 3x effect (BETTER_OFFER_PLANTED_BETTER = 3.0), and that bar has not been run.
findings.evidence: Probe using autonomy.experiments.sequential.half_width. Per-customer net simulated as a 5% buy rate x lognormal margin (mean 23.5, sd 124). 8k shop (about 360 per arm, 800 holdout): half-width `31.8 = 135% of mean net` at best tau, `459%` at tau = 10% of the mean. 300k shop (13,500 per arm): `5.5 = 23% of mean net`. grep shows .start/.review/.promote only in autonomy/experiments/gymrun.py:195,228,257. docs/v3/EXPERIMENTS.md:282-296 says the 9-of-10-seeds bar is unmeasured; autonomy/gym/scenarios.py BETTER_OFFER_PLANTED_BETTER = 3.0.
findings.real_world_impact: 8k shop: no experiment ever ends with a winner; every test times out with 'no clear winner, default stays'. 300k shop: only differences of 25% or more of profit per customer are found, while honest offer differences are 3-10% (CTO brief). Foundation C delivers briefing lines, not learning.
findings.recommendation: State the minimum detectable effect before registering and refuse tests that cannot reach it within max_days. Pool across weeks and goals, or use fixed-horizon tests on larger shares for small shops. Test the Gym bar with planted effects of 1.1-1.3x, not 3x. Wire start, review and promote and persist them, or remove the claim.

findings.assumption: Copy is written per customer type (50-300 types), a scoring model picks the top 3, and live tests cut losers (decision 6).
findings.problem: The type count is min(300, max(50, n/20)), so an 8k shop gets 300 types of about 27 customers, which is about 9 per live draft. A draft is cut only after 300 sends and non-overlapping z=3 Wilson bands, which needs thousands of sends per arm. Types are refitted weekly and content ids change weekly, so a live test never accumulates. 2,400 LLM drafts a week, plus a new WhatsApp template name per type per week, each needing Meta approval. CopyPlanner is not called from anywhere outside autonomy/content. The word-count features use [A-Za-z'], so Hindi in Devanagari counts 0 words.
findings.evidence: Probe with CopyConfig defaults: `customers 8000 types 300 members/type 26.7 members/draft(top3) 8.9`; `customers 300000 types 300 members/type 1000`. Cut thresholds via autonomy.content.live.wilson_bounds at z=3: `leader 0.04 loser 0.02 cut possible at sends/arm 5000`, `leader 0.03 loser 0.02 ... 10000`, `leader 0.022 loser 0.02 no cut even at 50000/arm`. autonomy/content/types.py:200-201; autonomy/content/config.py:18-29,65-72; docs/v3/COPY.md:48-52,171; autonomy/content/scoring.py `_WORD`.
findings.real_world_impact: 8k shop: a large weekly LLM bill for copy that is never evaluated; the marketer cannot review 2,400 drafts in 30 minutes. 300k shop: about 333 recipients per draft per week, so no draft is ever cut. WhatsApp: hundreds of template submissions a week against Meta's template limits and quality ratings.
findings.recommendation: Size types by statistical power, not headcount (for example 1-5 types under 50k customers). Keep types stable across weeks. Cut on pooled evidence across types. Treat WhatsApp templates as a slow, small, human-approved set.

findings.assumption: The profile reaches every decision, and v3 should beat the best simple policy where customer features carry signal (MegaFon, Criteo), as v2's T-learner did (plan-v3 decision 1 pass test).
findings.problem: The look-alike model's inputs are CustomerState fields plus state.features, which come from events only. Non-event customer attributes (bench features, CRM fields such as age, city, tier or gender) arrive as `preferences` and are never read, except the single key no_discounts (features.py:518). In the real bench, Criteo and MegaFon customers have only SIGNUP and CONSENT events (adapters.py:539-552), so every customer looks identical to the v3 crowd.
findings.evidence: Probe: two CustomerStates with very different preferences {'X_1': '5.2', ...} and {'X_1': '-9.0', ...}: the look-alike base profiles are identical in every column (the only 'difference' was NaN tenure in both), and `52-feature profile identical from bench pre_events: True`. scripts/v2_realbench/common.py:215-217 ('handed to the agent's states as preferences'); scripts/v2_realbench/adapters.py:539-552.
findings.real_world_impact: The plan's headline real-data bar (beat the T-learner on MegaFon and Criteo) is unattainable by construction, so the pending CI run will fail for a structural reason, not a tuning one. For a 300k shop with a CRM team, all customer attributes are ignored.
findings.recommendation: Add a typed, approved path for static customer attributes into the profile (numeric plus one-hot, with point-in-time stamps), or drop the MegaFon and Criteo claims for v3.

findings.assumption: High leaving risk plus positive uplift means 'act now'; leaving risk raises urgency (decision 1).
findings.problem: Urgency is multiplied by 1 + 0.5 x churn_risk regardless of measured uplift. On an orders-only D2C shop, churn risk is mostly recency, and most customers are 'at risk', so most bids are scaled up by about 1.4x. This adds to the known expected-value overestimate (v2 is still 1.46x). It is a hand-set prior, not learned; churn risk is not uplift (the plan itself says uplift is what matters). Separately, with no margin in the file, clv_90d is trained in revenue (margin rate 1.0) while ValueModel values a conversion at margin 0.4, and future_value returns clv_90d directly. Two units are mixed in the attention price and in who's cost ceiling.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Marketing-ai-/b3510c52-036a-5471-a52e-fd5d81ce4bd7/scratchpad/redteam/slow_probe.py (2,000 customers, 35% repeaters, 14 months, no margin): `RiskCheck(passed=True, auc=0.83...)`, `risk scored 1198 mean 0.71 p10 0.43 p50 0.83 p90 0.96`, so the median urgency multiplier is 1.41. `clv_90d mean 552 (REVENUE units, no margin in file)`. Code: autonomy/decide/who.py:79-80; autonomy/decide/slow_models.py:143-146,163-182 (rate 1 when no margin); autonomy/decide/models.py:279-303.
findings.real_world_impact: The agent sends more, mostly to customers who are naturally lapsing (where uplift is often lowest), and quotes bigger expected profits. The calibration gate the plan demands (within 1.5x) gets harder to meet.
findings.recommendation: Remove the fixed multiplier; let risk enter only as a feature of the uplift model, and keep it only if held-out uplift by risk tier supports it. Make the value label and ValueModel use the same margin assumption, and flag when it is assumed.

findings.assumption: Sleeping dogs are found from each customer's own buying around messages, pooled by traits (ContactHarm/TraitHarm); the holdout corrects for seasonal trend.
findings.problem: The harm ratio compares a customer's purchases in message weeks with their other weeks (bidders.py:572-576). The holdout corrects only for a segment-level organic trend, but v3 decides *when* to message on predicted propensity. Leaving-risk urgency concentrates sends on customers whose own buying is declining, so their message weeks have fewer purchases: false sleeping dogs, and the agent then leaves alone exactly the lapsing customers it meant to save. Refill moments send just before a predicted purchase, so message weeks have more purchases and real sleeping dogs are masked. The 'traits' are keyed partly on load, i.e. the agent's own contact volume (who.py:118-133, with a freeze to stop oscillation).
findings.evidence: autonomy/decide/bidders.py:562-612 (outcome = share of own purchases in exposed weeks; trend from holdout per starting segment); autonomy/decide/who.py:79 (risk_urgency), 118-133 (TraitKeys including load); docs/v3/MOMENTS.md:70-72 (refill window). No within-person propensity adjustment exists. Analysis, not run end to end (a Gym run of more than 200x14 was out of budget).
findings.real_world_impact: Under the full preset, the harm readings of v2 and v3 drift in directions set by v3's own targeting. A marketer sees 'left alone: likely annoyed by messages' for customers who were simply lapsing.
findings.recommendation: Read harm only from randomised exposure (holdout, exploration-floor sends weighted by logged propensity), as the look-alike model already does. Add a Gym scenario where sends correlate with propensity and no harm is planted, and require zero false flags.

findings.assumption: Proof, experiments and auto-budget measure incremental profit.
findings.problem: Rewards never subtract refunds ('Refunds are not subtracted yet', proof/rewards.py:60), although the Shopify connector already emits REFUND events for voids naming the order (connectors/shopify/mapping.py:7,178-186). Experiments (reading.collect_outcomes) and auto-budget (budget/rebalance.goal_returns) read the same rewards.
findings.evidence: autonomy/proof/rewards.py:60; autonomy/experiments/reading.py:105-148; autonomy/budget/rebalance.py:1-20; autonomy/connectors/shopify/mapping.py:7,178-186.
findings.real_world_impact: India D2C: cash-on-delivery orders returned undelivered often run 20-30%, and discount-driven impulse COD orders return more. Offer arms and WhatsApp journeys are credited with orders that never paid, and auto-budget would move money toward them.
findings.recommendation: Net refunds and voids by order_id (already present on both events) within the reward window before any proof, experiment or budget reading; report the gross-to-net gap.

findings.assumption: The product says plainly which level a shop is at (plan-v3 section 6: 'Your shop is small, so I start from what works for similar shops').
findings.problem: No such message exists. Gate states (look-alike ready or not, slow-model check failed or passed, scoring model trusted, moments dormant for lack of events or country, journeys dropping channels as never read) are not surfaced in the briefing, inbox or UI. Every fallback is silent by design ('exactly the prior'). Moments' reasons are filled but not shown (MOMENTS.md 'Explanations carry the reasons, the UI does not show them yet').
findings.evidence: grep -rniE 'shop is small|data level|honest level' autonomy api: no matches. grep of autonomy/inbox, autonomy/agents and api for lookalike, churn_risk or WhoBook finds only analyst.py (early-signal section). autonomy/inbox/briefing.py additions concern budget moves only. docs/v3/MOMENTS.md 'Open (for the integrator)'.
findings.real_world_impact: An 8k shop turns on AUTONOMY_V3 and believes it has 'look-alike learning, leaving risk, moments, experiments'. In practice it gets the v2 click model, a recency multiplier, payday and festival multipliers for everyone, and email turned off for non-clickers, with no way to tell.
findings.recommendation: Add a weekly 'what is actually on' section: for each part, ready or not, why not, and what data would turn it on (for example 'need 60 holdout outcomes, have 22'; 'no cart or view events received').

findings.assumption: AUTONOMY_V3 suits small to mid-size shops; the 300k end of the target is fine with the batched sweep (PRESET.md, SCALE.md).
findings.problem: WhoBook keeps every event of every customer handed to it, all types, in memory, per goal (who.py:351-360), and refits the slow models on all of them (who.py:377). The profile's 1M-customer pass test was not run (PROFILE.md:241).
findings.evidence: Probe: a pydantic Event with a timezone attr is about 1,685 bytes (`bytes per Event ~ 1685`). autonomy/decide/who.py:334,351-360,377; docs/v3/WHO.md:205; docs/v3/PROFILE.md:241-249.
findings.real_world_impact: 300k shop, 3 years, app events: tens of millions of events, i.e. tens of GB per goal, plus agent SEND, DELIVER and CLICK events growing every day. The worker runs out of memory. Even orders-only, the store grows with every send.
findings.recommendation: Feed the slow models from training_rows_from_store (it already exists) on a weekly job, keep only the per-customer digests in memory, and give the preset a measured customer ceiling.

findings.assumption: Moments (view, cart, refill, price drop, payday, festival) make messages land; 'the response model learns what a message earns at these moments' (MOMENTS.md:78).
findings.problem: For an orders-only shop, view, cart and price-drop moments never fire, and price drops have no producer at all. What remains is payday on the 1st and last of the month for everyone, festivals for everyone (only if AUTONOMY_COUNTRIES names exactly one country; Shopify mapping sets no country), and a buying-rhythm fallback for customers with 3 or more purchase days. The multipliers are fixed priors applied outside every response model. No model has a moment feature, so the 'learns' claim is false. The India calendar has dates for 2026 and 2027 only, then moments end silently.
findings.evidence: configs/v3/moments.yaml (multipliers 1.15-1.6); grep 'moment' in autonomy/decide/lookalike.py and models.py shows no moment feature; autonomy/runtime/settings.py:343 (country only when len(countries)==1); configs/v3/calendar_in.yaml:17-18; docs/v3/MOMENTS.md:229, 236-239.
findings.real_world_impact: Small: by the docs' own account moments only re-rank when caps or budget bind. In practice it is a hidden 'send more around the 1st and around Diwali' rule with untested multipliers.
findings.recommendation: Either learn moment effects (a moment indicator in the uplift model, validated on the holdout) or label them as fixed business rules the marketer sets. Warn when the calendar has no future dates.

findings.assumption: v3 does not build its own file-to-customer logic; the Data Doctor's order-log path is the one front door and 'the agent reads what it builds' (plan-v3 1.1 and 7).
findings.problem: build_from_order_log is referenced only inside engine/doctor/order_log_workflow.py. Nothing in autonomy/ reads the order-log output. The v3 profile and slow models rebuild order grouping (order_id or invoice_no at the same instant) and month-end rows themselves from the event store (autonomy/profile/facts.py:15-18; slow_models.py). So the plan's identity and money rules live in two places again. Also the image check's '95% caught' is 100% by construction (fake model reads the fake provider's notes; IMAGES.md:168-176), with no real model, no scheduler and an in-memory queue.
findings.evidence: grep build_from_order_log: only engine/doctor/order_log_workflow.py; grep order_log in autonomy/: no matches; autonomy/profile/facts.py:15-18; docs/v3/IMAGES.md:164-176.
findings.real_world_impact: A shop whose order-log quirks the Doctor resolved (blank ids, returns without the C prefix) can still be profiled differently by the agent. The image pass test gives no evidence about real images.
findings.recommendation: Make the agent's profile read the Doctor's confirmed mapping, or drop the 'one front door' claim. Mark the image pass test 'not measured' until a real vision model is evaluated on real bad images.

Degrades silently | Ready, but wiped on each rebuild; CRM attributes ignored |

| Copy scoring + live cuts | past sends with 200/50 purchases; at least 300 sends per draft; Meta approvals; runtime wiring (absent) | 300 types of about 27 customers, 2,400 drafts a week, no cut ever; not wired | 333 per draft per week, no cut (about 5,000 needed per arm); template flood |
| Images | a real image and vision model (absent), scheduler (absent) | Not usable (fake provider) | Not usable |
| Early signals | history of first weeks, labels after 90 days, at least 3 scored months | Passes its backtest, then credits pull-forward as 90-day value (probe +₹103 per customer from a zero effect); not wired | Same bias, tighter (falsely confident) interval |
| Auto-budget | proofs with non-overlapping 95% ranges, both above 0 | Never moves (ranges overlap); not wired; a move would trigger a rebuild that wipes the learners | Rarely moves; reads gross orders (no refunds) |

B: Statistics and learning loops (identi.lens: B: Statistics and learning loops (identifiability, propensities, power, compounding multipliers, Gym circularity)
B: Statistics and learning loops (identi.summary: Through a statistics lens, v3 adds many learned-looking parts on top of v2. v2 was already about 10x overconfident, and none of these parts gives the agent a better-identified causal signal. The one new causal learner, the look-alike crowd, compares contacted customers with the 10% holdout. Its profile includes contact-history columns (contacts_7d/30d, per-channel delivered/idle) that are zero for every holdout customer by construction. So once the agent is running, uplift becomes unidentified: a probe at 8k customers with zero true effect gave -4.1pp ± 11.8pp. Even with those columns equalised, its posterior sd is 1-2pp, against honest effects of 0.1-0.5pp. A 40k-row cap, filled by daily holdout rows, holds its control evidence near ~2.7k effective windows whether the shop has 8k or 300k customers. Its per-person response shift cannot be identified either: agent customers never have their own control windows, so the shift absorbs organic buying. v3 then multiplies the learned net by fixed, never-learned factors: moments up to 2.5x and leaving risk up to 1.5x. These are applied before an attention price that is not scaled, so they do turn losing messages into sends, which contradicts PRESET.md. No runtime calibration gate exists. Moments also time sends to when people would buy anyway, and that breaks the within-person harm ratio the sleeping-dog logic depends on: in a stylised probe a true 0.6 dog reads as about 22. The measurement layer (live experiments, auto-budget, early signals, copy elimination) is not wired. Even if wired, it cannot detect realistic effects below roughly 300k customers. The Gym cannot settle any of this: it plants per-contact relative lifts of 67-350% (the brief's honest figure is 3-10%), uses the agent's own multiplicative factor structure, puts cart effects on uplift only, has no seasonality, and gives at-risk customers the largest lift, which is exactly the leaving-risk heuristic. Several pieces are statistically careful and are listed under sound, but the core "learns who and when to contact" claim is not supported at target data sizes.
sound: Randomisation and proof accounting: hash-based holdout/baseline split, intent-to-treat rewards that keep undelivered sends, and a last-touch cutoff applied the same to every group so agent customers do not get extra counted days (autonomy/proof/rewards.py docstring, split.py).

The look-alike model refuses profiles taken after their window opened, fits only closed windows, and never treats the agent's own 'do nothing' as a control (lookalike.py:916-925, OutcomeBook docstring; agent.py _remember).

Logged propensities count the exploration floor exactly (floor/n + (1-floor) x Thompson share), the real draw is one of the Monte Carlo draws, and journey later steps are kept out of response learning (policy.py:188-234; PRESET.md 'Journeys and learning').

Live experiments use mSPRT always-valid intervals with a Bonferroni split over the 2k-1 comparisons of each look, which handles peeking within one experiment (experiments/sequential.py, reading.py:alpha_each).
The live copy cut rule (non-overlapping 3-sigma Wilson bands, the leader is never cut) is conservative and resists peeking; it trades power for safety (content/live.py).
Slow models are point-in-time, with censoring and a purge between training and held-out month (slow_models.py docstring).
Warm-start calibration from history only accepts campaigns that show real randomisation (equal logged propensities, pool-size and balance checks) (learning/calibration.py:12-31).
The docs are honest that nothing in v3 is proven yet and that experiments, early signals and auto-budget are not wired (STATUS.md 'Not proven yet', PRESET.md).

findings.assumption: The look-alike crowd learns uplift (treated vs control) from the agent's sends plus the 10% holdout, given the customer's profile (LOOKALIKE.md Method 2; lookalike.py:7-17).
findings.problem: The profile it conditions on has post-treatment columns: contacts_7d, contacts_30d and, per channel, delivered/click_rate/idle (lookalike.py:68-89, 136-148). Holdout customers are never contacted, so after launch these are 0 or capped for every control row and non-zero for most treated rows. The baseline's profile slopes (ridge sd 1) can then separate holdout from contacted rows, and the 'contacted' term is identified only by extrapolation and the prior. Uplift becomes noise, or is biased.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Marketing-ai-/b3510c52-036a-5471-a52e-fd5d81ce4bd7/scratchpad/redteam/p1_lookalike.py (real LookalikeResponseModel, 8,000 customers, 10% holdout, 3 monthly windows, TRUE uplift 0). With contacts_30d=0 for the holdout and 1 for contacted rows: 'mean uplift/msg=-4.07pp, median sd=11.77pp'. The same data with contact columns equalised (p1b_samecontacts.py): '-0.08pp, sd 1.57pp'. Seed sweep with equalised columns, null effect: 30k customers -1.41/+1.26/+0.78/+0.01pp (sd ~1.1pp); 8k +0.69/-1.78/-1.60pp (sd 1.2-1.9pp).
findings.real_world_impact: 8k-customer Shopify/Klaviyo shop: after the first month every agent customer has contacts_30d>=1 and every holdout customer has 0, so the crowd's estimate has sd of about 12pp. precision_blend then weights it at about 1/144 of the click prior, so the agent runs on the v2 click model (the one 10x overconfident on Hillstrom) while the UI reports look-alike learning. At 300k it is no better (see B2). Even in the best case, a 1-2pp sd cannot resolve honest effects of 0.1-0.5pp (3-10% of a 1-5% base).
findings.recommendation: Remove every column that the policy determines after launch (contact counts, delivered, idle, click-rate-since-launch) from the treated-vs-control model, or freeze them at the pre-launch value for both groups. Add a test where the holdout's contact columns differ, as they do live. Report the crowd's posterior sd per action in the briefing, and treat the look-alike as not ready while that sd is larger than the effect sizes the business cares about.

findings.assumption: Bigger shops give the look-alike crowd more evidence; max_rows=40,000 'bounds the memory and the cost of a refit' (lookalike.py:265-266).
findings.problem: The runtime decides on every holdout customer every day. OutcomeBook keeps each holdout 'do nothing' as a control window with overlap weight 1/7 (7-day horizon, agent.py:204, lookalike.py:982-995). The 40k newest-row cap therefore holds a few days of data at mid-market size and under a day at 300k. Effective control evidence stays near ~2.7k windows whatever the shop size, and the crowd keeps forgetting.
findings.evidence: Probe p3_power.py: 'N=8,000: rows/day ~1,714; cap holds ~23.3 days; effective control windows ~2,667'; 'N=50,000: ~3.7 days; ~2,667'; 'N=300,000: rows/day ~64,286; cap holds ~0.6 days; ~2,667'. Real model at 30k customers with 4 sends/month (rows exceed the cap): median posterior sd 5.4-6.0pp and per-message estimates 1.86/-0.55/+3.77pp across 3 seeds (true marginal 0.5pp), against ~1.1pp sd at 1 send/month.
findings.real_world_impact: A 300k-customer brand with a CRM team gets look-alike precision no better than an 8k shop's, refreshed from the last ~15 hours of closed windows. Seasonal swings (Diwali week vs the week after) dominate whatever the crowd reads.
findings.recommendation: Store aggregated control rows: one control window per holdout customer per horizon, not one per daily sweep. Subsample treated rows rather than holdout rows. Size the cap from the shop's holdout, not as a constant. Add a unit test of crowd precision against customer count.

findings.assumption: Moments and leaving-risk urgency are 'starting priors' that 'the response model learns' (configs/v3/moments.yaml header, MOMENTS.md:78-79), and 'a high risk or a live cart never turns a losing message into a winner' (PRESET.md:87).
findings.problem: (a) Nothing learns the multipliers. moments.py is 'Pure and deterministic: no clock reads, no randomness' and no code updates them. WhoConfig.risk_urgency=0.5 is a constant (who.py:79, 479-484). (b) They multiply the response model's output, net = urgency x (uplift x value - offer cost - channel cost) (bidders.py:1719-1721, 1793). That model already learned from sends made at moments and from high-risk customers, so these effects are counted twice. (c) The auction then subtracts an attention price that is NOT scaled by urgency: means = expected_net - cost(b) (policy.py:407, 174-178). So urgency up to 2.5 x 1.5 = 3.75 does turn a message below the attention price into a send, contrary to the doc. (d) No runtime calibration gate exists: LookalikeResponseModel.calibration() is called only in the non-collected scripts tests/v3/lookalike/gym_run.py:35 and bench_run.py:26. The 'within 1.5x' bar is checked only in a CI bench run.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic on the code path: base net 0.5, attention price 1.0 -> loses; with urgency 3.75 -> 1.875 - 1.0 > 0 -> wins. grep for any learner of moment multipliers or calibration guard in autonomy/runtime, autonomy/inbox: none. LIFT_PER_CLICK_PRIOR=(0.25,0.25) is unchanged (agent.py:485), the prior learning/calibration.py:4-6 itself names as the cause of v2's ~10x overvaluation.
findings.real_world_impact: Indian D2C shop with default_country=IN: during each festival window every customer gets x1.25-1.7. Payday (1st and last of month) adds x1.15, and high-risk lapsers x1.5, on top of a click model that starts at a quarter purchase per click. In the weeks when inboxes and WhatsApp are most crowded the agent sends more, with nothing that measures whether the festival multiplier was right. Errors compound: a 10x model error times 3.75 is up to 37x.
findings.recommendation: Make each multiplier a learned coefficient: a moment indicator in the effect term, estimated against holdout customers who were in the same moment, starting at 1 and capped by its posterior. Scale the attention price by the same urgency, or apply urgency only to the uplift term. Add a runtime guard: when expected incremental value per message exceeds the agent-vs-holdout measured value by more than kx, shrink all bids and alert.

findings.assumption: The Gym (plus the real bench) can show that v3 beats v2 and the best simple rule (STATUS.md 'Not proven yet', PRESET.md 'The comparison: pending CI').
findings.problem: The Gym's truths are planted by the same authors, in the agent's own functional form, at effect sizes far from the brief's. (1) Planted relative lift per contact: researcher email 0.004/day against organic 0.006/day (+67%); at_risk 0.005-0.007 against 0.002 (+250-350%); offers multiply by up to 2.5. The CTO brief's honest figure is 3-10%. (2) Lift = uplift[ch] x offer_mult x theme_mult x hour x fatigue x moment (truth.py:563-566): the same separable factorisation as ClickResponseModel (segment rate x channel x offer x theme). (3) A cart or refill raises only the contact's lift, never organic buying (truth.py:355-370, 565-566). In reality cart abandoners and refill-due customers buy on their own at high rates. (4) Moment multiplier 3.0 with a 1-day half-life and a 3-day refill lead mirror the agent's 1.6/1.0/3.0 config. (5) There is no seasonality, festival or payday (grep 'season|festival|payday' in autonomy/gym finds only a note that Gym customers get none). (6) at_risk has the highest planted relative lift, which is exactly what risk urgency assumes. (7) The real bench makes one decision per customer, so journeys, frequency plans and moments are dormant there (PRESET.md 'What the preset does not fix').
findings.evidence: autonomy/gym/api.py:74-84 (daily_purchase_rate researcher 0.006, at_risk 0.002, loyal 0.02); autonomy/gym/scenarios.py:231-244 (_BASE_CHANNEL_UPLIFT), 433-443 (moments_planted cart_lift_multiplier=3.0, refill_lead_days=3.0); truth.py:563-566.
findings.real_world_impact: A green Gym CI run for agent_v3 says only that the agent finds effects shaped like its own assumptions, at 10-50x realistic size. No CI path tests the v3 parts that matter most (moments, journeys, frequency holds) against data the authors did not design. Shipping on that evidence repeats v2, which the Gym passed and real randomised data did not support (REAL_DATA_RESULTS.md).
findings.recommendation: Add adversarial Gym scenarios: lifts of 3-10% relative; carts and refills that raise organic buying with zero or negative incremental lift; festival seasonality in organic rates with no extra lift; at_risk with the lowest lift; additive or interaction truths the agent's factorisation cannot express. Require v3 to do no harm there. Get one randomised real-data test where moments/journeys can act (e.g. a pilot with a 50/50 v2-vs-v3 split) before claiming gains.

findings.assumption: ContactHarm / TraitHarm detect sleeping dogs from 'the share [of purchases] made in the week after a message', with odds = ratio x exposed/open days, 'so how much someone buys in general cancels out' (bidders.py:572-575; who.py:15-28).
findings.problem: This within-person estimator is valid only if send timing is independent of when the customer would buy anyway. v3 moments time sends to exactly those moments: refill_due opens 3 days before the usual gap (with a rhythm fallback for 'any repeat buyer near their average gap', MOMENTS.md:233-234), plus payday, festivals, carts and returns after absence. Exposed weeks then hold organically likely purchases, so the ratio is pushed far above 1 and real harm is hidden. TraitHarm also groups customers by 'how many messages they had last month' (who.py:20-21, load_cut), a trait the agent's own policy sets.
findings.evidence: Stylised probe p2_harm_timing.py (purchases on a 30-day rhythm ±2 days, zero message effect, or a true 0.6 dog): 'true ratio 1.00: untimed sends -> read 1.01; moment-timed sends -> read 36.01'; 'true ratio 0.60 (sleeping dog): untimed -> 0.60; moment-timed -> 22.19'. The size is exaggerated by the stylised rhythm, but the direction is certain.
findings.real_world_impact: A shop selling consumables (skincare, pet food, coffee) with moments on: replenishment customers who resent messages look strongly helped by them. They keep being messaged, unsubscribe on WhatsApp, and the number's quality rating falls. The v2 safeguard against sleeping dogs is silently disabled by the v3 feature meant to add value.
findings.recommendation: Read harm only against the holdout (agent-group vs holdout purchase rates by trait band), or compare exposed and open windows only on sends whose timing was randomised (e.g. a random-day exploration slice). Never mix moment-timed sends into the within-person ratio. Remove policy-determined traits from the grouping.

findings.assumption: Each message's uplift is learned against the holdout and priced per message (OutcomeBook; LiftPerClick 'extra purchases per click').
findings.problem: The holdout is 'never contacted', so the comparison measures the effect of being in a contact regime. OutcomeBook credits every send's 7-day window with any purchase in it, overlap-weighted only (lookalike.py:969-981, 989-995). LiftPerClick divides the total agent-vs-holdout extra purchases by total clicks (agent.py:955-974, 1000-1013), an average rather than a marginal effect. When messages saturate, the 2nd-4th message of a week or month is credited with the whole regime's effect, and the auction then prices each extra message at that average.
findings.evidence: p1b_samecontacts.py 'regime' scenario (any contact in a 30-day window adds +1pp; 4 sends per window; contact columns equalised so B1 does not interfere): 'mean uplift/msg=0.89pp' at 8k. The true marginal per message is 0.25pp (1pp/4), so the 2nd-4th messages are overvalued about 3.5x.
findings.real_world_impact: With a weekly or more frequent cadence, the agent keeps finding the next message worth sending. This is the 'contacts 94-97%, behaves like send-to-all' failure of v2, and journeys and urgency now push it further.
findings.recommendation: Estimate a dose-response: randomise contact frequency (e.g. 1 vs 2 vs 4 per month) inside a slice of the agent group and fit marginal lift per extra message. Until then, discount each extra message in a window by a conservative prior on diminishing returns.

findings.assumption: Per-customer learning: 'a customer with thirty rows mostly follows their own record' for their response to contact (lookalike.py:28-33).
findings.problem: Groups are fixed, so an agent-group customer never has their own control windows (the agent's own 'do nothing' is deliberately not kept). Their baseline shift u and response shift v come from the same residuals: _rebuild_people sets s_all == s_t for them (lookalike.py:762-787, 822-838). The 2x2 solve splits the residual by the prior variances, so part of a customer's organic propensity is labelled 'responds to messages'. This is the targeting confound the lens asks about: the agent contacts people who would buy anyway and learns they are persuadable. It matches docs/research/v2/data/00_VERDICT.md (per-person learning fails even at enterprise scale).
findings.evidence: Probes with ZERO true uplift: corr(person response shift v, latent organic propensity z) = 0.20/0.17/0.13 at 8k and 0.08-0.13 at 30k (p1b output lines). The effect variance is also estimated as est_t - sigma_base, clipped at 0.01 (lookalike.py:779-781), so it depends on the arbitrary split.
findings.real_world_impact: Loyal customers who buy anyway slowly gain higher predicted uplift, get more messages and offers (with the who cost ceiling keyed to their high clv_90d), and the money goes to sure things.
findings.recommendation: Drop the per-person response shift, or estimate it only from customers who were randomised in and out of contact over time (a rotating per-person micro-holdout). Keep the per-person baseline shift, which is identified.

findings.assumption: precision_blend combines the click model and the look-alike crowd 'by precision (inverse variance)' as two independent estimates (lookalike.py:281-288, 445-451).
findings.problem: Both are calibrated on the same agent-vs-holdout comparison. LiftPerClick scales the click model by agent-group minus holdout purchases (agent.py:880-1013), and the crowd's contact effect is identified only by the same holdout. Inverse-variance blending of correlated estimates understates the sd (by up to about sqrt(2) when both rely mainly on the holdout) and Thompson sampling explores too little. LiftPerClick also truncates at 0 (agent.py:1013, max(...,0)), which biases it upward in a null-effect shop.
findings.evidence: Code references above. LiftPerClick.posterior and LookalikeResponseModel.fit both read the same Group.HOLDOUT customers (agent.py:963-970; OutcomeBook.remember accepts only Group.HOLDOUT NOTHING as control, lookalike.py:918-921).
findings.real_world_impact: The briefing shows tighter ranges than the data supports, and restraint (margin_fn) lets more sends through, which adds to the overconfidence v2 already had.
findings.recommendation: Use one estimator of the treated-vs-control scale and let the other only reorder options. Or blend with an assumed correlation, or bootstrap the whole pipeline over holdout customers to get an honest joint sd.

findings.assumption: Live experiments, auto-budget and early signals let the agent 'test itself' and move money to what works (plan-v3 §3.C, §8; DECISIONS V-3, V-4).
findings.problem: (1) Not wired: outside autonomy/experiments/ only an empty ExperimentBook() is built (runtime/v3.py:123), nothing calls rebalance/plan_move or the early-signal fit outside its own modules (only agents/analyst.py takes them as arguments), and the copy pipeline (LiveBoard/CopyPlanner/ScoringModel) is imported nowhere outside autonomy/content. (2) If wired, it is underpowered at target sizes: the V-3 cap gives 10% of the agent group across at most 2 arms per experiment, intervals are always-valid (1.55-1.9x wider), alpha is split by 3, and max_days defaults to 28. (3) Per-goal proof refuses when goals share customers (proof/estimate.py docstring), so in a normal multi-goal shop auto-budget has no input. Where it has input, it compares extremes chosen by point estimate, weekly, with single-look 95% intervals. (4) Early signals forecast 90-day margin from first-week behaviour, validated on observational history. That is a surrogate endpoint: an offer that pulls orders forward moves week-1 signals without moving 90-day margin, and the backtest cannot detect this.
findings.evidence: p3_power.py (80% power, alpha 0.05): agent vs holdout MDE at 8k = 2.06pp on a 4%/28-day base (51% relative), 1.14pp on 1.2%/7-day (95%). Experiment arm vs reference at 8k, 320 per arm: 6.59pp (165%) / 3.66pp (305%). At 50k: 2.64pp (66%). At 300k, 12,000 per arm: 1.08pp (27%) / 0.60pp (50%). Copy elimination (3-sigma Wilson, 1.0% vs 1.5% per send) needs about 17,700 sends per draft; an 8k shop with 6 types x 3 drafts sends about 350 per draft per week, so about 50 weeks.
findings.real_world_impact: 8k shop: every experiment ends 'no_winner' after 28 days, which is safe but teaches nothing, and the 'agent runs its own experiments' story is empty. 300k shop: only effects of 27-50% relative or more are detectable, against real differences between offers of 5-10%. Wired as is, the early-signal model would credit discount arms with pull-forward.
findings.recommendation: State minimum shop sizes per feature in the UI and refuse to start a test whose MDE exceeds a plausible effect (compute MDE before registration). Pool experiment learning across clients via the priors. Validate early signals as a surrogate on randomised history (does the treatment effect on the signal predict the treatment effect on 90-day margin?) before any use. Make auto-budget use always-valid intervals and require non-overlapping per-goal holdouts.

findings.assumption: Leaving risk predicts who to act on: urgency x (1 + 0.5 x churn_risk), used only after a held-out check (who.py:5-12; slow_models.py:29-37).
findings.problem: Churn risk is a prediction of outcome, not of uplift. Retention research (e.g. Ascarza 2018) finds the highest-risk customers are often not the most persuadable, and v3 hard-codes the opposite. The gate checks only discrimination (AUC >= 0.60 on as few as 40 held-out rows, with as few as 3 leavers) and never whether risk-weighted targeting earns more. Once the agent runs, the model retrains on labels the agent's own messages changed (who.py: WhoBook refits at month-ends on all held events), creating a feedback loop: successful retention lowers the predicted risk of the features it targeted.
findings.evidence: Null-model probe: P(AUC >= 0.60 | useless scores) = 0.30 with 3 leavers/37 stayers, 0.18 with 10/30, 0.15 with 10/140. Real recency alone easily exceeds 0.6, so the gate passes for reasons unrelated to whether urgency helps. The Gym plants at_risk with the largest relative lift (+250-350%, gym/api.py:80, scenarios.py:240), so the Gym confirms the heuristic by construction.
findings.real_world_impact: The 14-month Shopify shop sends more, and makes costlier offers, to lapsing one-time buyers, the group with the lowest real response. This raises unsubscribe and complaint pressure where it is least valuable.
findings.recommendation: Turn risk_urgency off by default. Learn a risk x contact interaction in the uplift model against the holdout, and use it only if its posterior is credibly positive. Raise the AUC gate's sample minimums, or use a CI-based gate.

findings.assumption: Clicks are a clean, fast proxy for response ('the people a message moves are the people who click', agent.py:541-576), and personal click factors pick out responsive customers.
findings.problem: There is no bot or security-scanner click filtering anywhere in autonomy/ (grep 'bot click|scanner|apple mail|mpp' finds only PII scanners in engine/). Scanner clicks are concentrated on particular addresses (corporate gateways), so PersonalEffects marks those customers as highly responsive and sends to them more. LiftPerClick then divides real extra purchases by inflated clicks, which mutes every honest click. ch_open_rate (MPP-inflated) is also a profile feature fed to the crowd and tiredness models (profile/features.py:413-418).
findings.evidence: grep -rn -i 'bot click|bot_click|scanner|machine open|apple mail|mpp' autonomy engine -> only engine/pii.py and redaction text scanners. ClickResponseModel docstring (agent.py:541-576) and PersonalEffects (models.py:647-670) take clicks at face value.
findings.real_world_impact: Klaviyo shop: customers whose mail passes a link-scanning gateway look like the best responders and get the most emails and offers. Real buyers' click signal is diluted. Thompson exploration chases scanner-driven 'winning' themes.
findings.recommendation: Filter clicks within N seconds of delivery, clicks on every link at once, and known scanner user agents/IPs before they reach any model. Drop open-rate features. Report the share of clicks filtered.

findings.assumption: Contacted rows weighted by 1/logged propensity correct for the agent's targeting (lookalike.py:22-25, 520-540).
findings.problem: The weight uses the probability of the specific action chosen (Decision.probability), not the probability of being contacted at all. That is the relevant propensity for the treated-vs-control balance, the only one the holdout can identify. With up to 10 options and a 5% floor, the floor term is 0.005, so weights often hit ipw_clip=20 and are then self-normalised, adding noise and bias towards customers with many near-equal options (multi-channel consents). Experiment rows log the within-arm probability (experiments/policy.py:16-26), mixing conditional and unconditional propensities in one fit. Frequency-plan holds and plausible_z pruning give deterministic zero-probability actions (policy.py:771-786), so off-policy evaluation of any policy that would send on those days has no support.
findings.evidence: policy.py:109-111 (floor 0.05, max options 10), 232; lookalike.py:255-256 (ipw_clip 20), 528-533.
findings.real_world_impact: Mostly extra variance in an estimator that is already underpowered. Off-policy reads of 'what if we had not held' are unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Log and use P(contact | x) (the sum over acting options) for the contact term. Keep per-action probabilities for the level terms. Mark rows with deterministic holds as unusable for OPE in the log.

findings.assumption: The tiredness model learns per-profile tolerance from lost contacts (frequency.py:7-20; min_events=20).
findings.problem: Lost-contact events are rare and partly invisible. Gmail sends no per-recipient spam complaints to a feedback loop. A WhatsApp opt-out appears only as error 131050 on the next send attempt (whatsapp.py:51-53, 289-294), so the loss is logged at a later send, not the one that caused it. The crowd's Poisson regression over the full profile (base plus about 52 nightly features) switches on at 20 events, with ridge sd 0.3 per feature.
findings.evidence: frequency.py ToleranceConfig: min_events=20.0, slope_penalty=10.0; COMPLAINT_BASE_RATE=0.0005 (agent.py:1133). At a 0.2% unsubscribe rate an 8k shop sending weekly sees about 16 events a week, so the crowd fits on a few dozen events over ~50+ features.
findings.real_world_impact: Tiredness multipliers mostly fit noise, bounded only by the [1/max, max] clamp. WhatsApp fatigue (blocks and reports) mostly reaches the business only as a number-level quality drop, which the breakers handle but the per-customer model never sees.
findings.recommendation: Raise min_events to a few hundred, fit on a handful of pre-chosen features, attribute a 131050 opt-out to the previous delivered message, and say in the UI that complaint data from Gmail is missing.

B: Statistics and learning loops (identi.minimal_data_table:
| v3 learning piece | 8k-customer D2C (14 mo Shopify, Klaviyo, WhatsApp templates, no views/carts/margin) | 300k-customer brand (3 yrs, app events, CRM team) |

Confirmed: never_read (journeys.py:338-349) counts only clicks and replies against stats.sends ≥ 5 (configs/v3/journeys.yaml:16). expand() drops both journeys and single bids on such channels (journeys.py:413-414, 424-429), so the docstring's 'never takes a channel away' (journeys.py:26-27) is false. I re-ran slow_probe.py and got the same result: RiskCheck passed (auc 0.83), churn_risk p50 0.83, so the median multiplier is 1.41. The code matches. The fixed hand-set factor 1 + 0.5 x risk is at who.py:79-80, 479-484, and is applied at bidders.py:1720-1721. With no margin data the slow models use margin rate 1.0 (slow_models.py:173-182), while ValueModel uses 0.4 (models.py:280-293), and future_value returns clv_90d as is (models.py:299-303). Two nuances. Urgency scales the whole net, urgency x (uplift x value - costs) (bidders.py:1793), so a bid's sign never flips. The effect is on ranking against the attention price, on the harm and stake terms (1845-1847), and on reported expected value; the claim that 'it sends more' is only at the margin. The unit mix also does not inflate uniformly: in the probe, clv_90d had a mean of 552 against a ValueModel fallback of 960. The mechanism is as described. ContactHarm reads a customer's share of purchases in exposed weeks against open days. The only correction is the holdout's organic trend per starting segment (bidders.py:562-612 docstring), with no adjustment for when the agent chose to send. TraitKeys includes load, the agent's own contact volume (who.py:118-133), which is acknowledged through the _frozen mechanism (who.py:340-345). The existing no-harm tests (tests/v2/contact_less/test_discounts_dogs.py:315; tests/v3/who/test_trait_harm.py:125) build evidence where exposure is independent of each person's time-varying propensity, so no test covers send-timing confounding. This is a real untested gap, but its size is not shown. There are mitigations the reviewer does not mention: credible-bound charging, cross-fitting and shrinkage, so noise alone does not produce flags. The same confound already existed in v2 win-back targeting; it is not new in v3.

The mechanism holds. profile_of puts contacts_7d, contacts_30d and per-channel delivered/click_rate/idle into the base profile (lookalike.py:68-89, 136-163). _design feeds the same z to the baseline slopes (ridge base_penalty 1) and to the contact term (lookalike.py:665-687, 718-724). OutcomeBook keeps only the holdout's NOTHING as control (lookalike.py:918-921). contacts_30d counts only SEND events (data/folder.py:257-264, 302-308), so holdout rows always read 0. The red team's 12pp sd comes from a worst case (every agent row at 1, every holdout row at 0, perfectly collinear). My variant uses 7-day windows, a null effect, 8k customers and agent contacts_30d drawn with some zeros (scratchpad/redteam/sk/b1var.py). Contact counts alone do little harm while early rows overlap: 'rare0' gives +0.33/+0.35pp with sd 0.6-1.1pp. Letting email delivers grow for agent rows only, as they do live, brings the bias back: 'rare0d' gives -2.07/-1.81pp with median sd 4.6/3.5pp (red team's setup at 4k: -2.7/-2.5pp, sd 5-6pp). B2's newest-rows cap removes the early overlapping rows, which makes it worse. One mitigation: a shop's own Klaviyo campaigns arrive as DELIVER for holdout customers too, which partly evens out the delivered column, but not contacts_30d or idle. In practice the precision blend weights the crowd near zero, so the agent falls back to the v2 click model rather than causing harm. Still, the core v3 claim of look-alike uplift learning does not hold in live use.

The daily sweep decides everyone in the audience (service.py:1834, 1861-1868). Holdout customers go through policy.decide and _remember every day (agent.py:2059-2065). OutcomeBook gives each consecutive control window an overlap weight of about 1/7 under the 7-day horizon (agent.py:204, lookalike.py:982-1000), but each one still takes a full row against max_rows=40,000. fit() then keeps only the newest usable rows (lookalike.py:512-516). So the effective number of control windows is set by the cap, not by shop size, and at 300k the cap covers about a day. The red team's arithmetic (about 1.7k rows/day at 8k, about 23 days of history) matches 800 daily holdout rows plus sends. Nothing aggregates the controls or sizes the cap from the holdout. It is not a blocker on its own, because the effect is lost precision and recency bias rather than wrong signs.

Confirmed: (a) no code learns the moment multipliers or risk_urgency. They are constants (moments.yaml header claims 'the response model learns'; who.py:79, 479-484). No runtime code calls calibration(); only tests/v3/lookalike/gym_run.py:35 and bench_run.py:26 do. (c) net = urgency*(uplift*value - offer_cost - cost) (bidders.py:1793), and the auction uses expected_net - cost(b), where the attention price is not scaled (policy.py:174-178, 407). So urgency can turn a positive net that is below the price into a winner. PRESET.md:87's justification ('both scale the whole net') only means the sign of net is kept, so the doc is misleading rather than strictly false. (b) Double counting is real, and more literal than stated: the nightly profile includes mom_cart_open, mom_days_since_cart and mom_refill_due_days (profile/features.py), so the look-alike can learn moment effects, and the fixed multiplier is then applied on top. Overstated: payday and festival need moments_country, which defaults to None (runtime/v3.py:60-62), so the Indian festival scenario requires the shop to set IN. The '10x times 3.75 = 37x' compounding is rhetoric, since LiftPerClick re-scales against the holdout over weeks, and the weekly cap and attention price still bound volume. This is mispricing that is not measured, not a non-working system, so major.

Confirmed: the planted lifts are huge relative to the brief's 3-10% (gym/api.py:74-80 organic researcher 0.006 and at_risk 0.002; scenarios.py:237-243 email uplift 0.004 and 0.005-0.007). The lift is a separable product of channel x offer x theme x hour x fatigue x moment (truth.py:563-566), which mirrors the agent's factorisation. There is no seasonality, festival or payday (gym/run.py:92). Carts never raise organic buying. Refuted or overstated: (3) refills DO buy organically. truth.py:56-58 says 'the world emits that purchase whatever is sent', and the lift applies only in the lead days before it. (4) The Gym's multipliers are 3.0 for both cart and refill, against the agent's 1.6 and 1.4, so only the shape is mirrored, not the magnitudes. Adversarial scenarios exist: null_effect, sleeping_dogs_15/hidden, discount_cannibalisation and drift_midway (scenarios.py registry). The docs admit the dormancy: PRESET.md:107-110 says moments are dormant in the Gym matrix and the bench makes one decision per customer, and STATUS.md says 'Nothing here shows yet that v3 beats the plain agent'. So it is not a false claim of proof. It is a real evidence gap: no scenario has realistic small positive lifts or organic-heavy moments, and nothing external tests moments or journeys. That makes it major (core claim unproven), not blocker.

The ContactHarm docstring states the within-person exposed/open odds design (bidders.py:572-575). Its only correction is a holdout-based organic trend per segment, which fixes season, not timing. The class (bidders.py:562 onward) has no exclusion for sends triggered by a moment, cart or refill. TraitHarm groups on 'how many messages they had last month' (who.py:20-21), a trait the policy sets. Moments time sends to likely organic purchases: refill_due opens 3 days before the due date, and cart_left fires right after a cart. That inflates the ratio. The direction is certain. The probe's 36x is from a stylised ±2-day rhythm with every send timed, while real timing tilt is partial (a 1.4x urgency multiplier, not a forced send). Cart-triggered decisions already existed in v2 (service.py trigger events), so the bias predates v3, but refill, payday and festival moments widen it.

The core holds. OutcomeBook credits each send's window with any purchase (tl.bought, lookalike.py:969-981), and the only adjustment is overlap. LiftPerClick divides total agent-minus-holdout extra purchases by total matured clicks (agent.py:966-1013), which is an average, not a marginal. There is no randomised dose-response. Overstated: the 0.89pp vs 0.25pp '3.5x' figure comes from a probe with 30-day windows and four overlapping sends per window. The live horizon is 7 days (agent.py:204), where weekly sends barely overlap and the bias takes a different shape (each message gets about a quarter of a monthly regime effect, still above a marginal of about 0 for the 2nd-4th message). Partial mitigations the finding omits: ClickResponseModel has a learned 'messages this week' fatigue factor (FATIGUE_STRENGTH, agent.py:518-519, _bucket), and the look-alike has effect slopes on contacts_7d/30d. Both are click-based or confounded (B1), so they do not replace a purchase dose-response.

I checked the algebra in _person (lookalike.py:822-838). For an agent-group customer every row is treated, so s_all == s_t and v_all == v_t (_rebuild_people, lookalike.py:762-767; the agent's own NOTHING is never kept, agent.py:2091-2107). Solving h=[[V+1/sb, V],[V, V+1/se]] against [s, s] gives v = (se/sb)*u. With the defaults sb=0.3 and se=0.1 (lookalike.py:270-272), a third of a customer's unexplained organic propensity is relabelled as response to contact. For p=5% and u=0.6, that adds about 0.95pp of predicted uplift, larger than honest effects. The sigma_effect estimate is est_t - sigma_base clipped at 0.01 (lookalike.py:779-781), so it rests on the same unidentified split. The probe's corr(v, z) of 0.1-0.2 under a null is consistent with this. The only exception is a customer who was a control in a past randomised campaign (warm start, agent.py:2353-2401). That case is rare.

Correct in principle. precision_blend assumes independence (lookalike.py:281-288, used at 445-451), while LiftPerClick (agent.py:955-1013) and the crowd's contact term are both identified from the same holdout. LiftPerClick.posterior truncates at 0 (max(...,0), agent.py:1013 and _ratio), which biases it upward in a null shop. The impact is overstated. Given B1/B2, the crowd's sd is usually several pp against the click model's roughly 1.25pp, so the crowd gets little blend weight and the variance understatement is far below sqrt(2) in practice. The truncation is also a deliberate guard against negative bids, and its bias is about 0.4 of an sd only when the true value is near 0.

Not wired, as claimed. runtime/v3.py:118-124 builds an empty ExperimentBook(). No code outside autonomy/experiments calls ExperimentBook.start (book.py:141). BudgetLedger.rebalance and plan_move are called only inside autonomy/budget. EarlySignal is referenced only in learning/early_signal.py and agents/analyst.py. Still, the 'agent tests itself' story is not working today. who.py:79 and 479-484 apply urgency 1 + 0.5*churn_risk, which is on in the v3 preset (runtime/v3.py:57). The gate is weaker than stated. slow_models.py:94-97 and 544-547 need 40 held-out rows, and the held-out minority-class minimum is max(min_class//4, 1) = 2, not 3. The gate checks only AUC >= 0.60 (slow_models.py:98, 552), never whether risk-weighted targeting earns more. Risk measures outcome, not persuadability, which is a real modelling gap. Retraining on outcomes the agent changed is a plausible feedback loop. In the Gym, at_risk has the largest relative planted lift (api.py:80 organic 0.002 vs scenarios.py:242 email 0.005 and WhatsApp 0.007), so the Gym confirms the heuristic by construction.

Confirmed: no filtering of bot or scanner clicks anywhere. A grep finds only PII scanners in engine/. The Klaviyo mapping turns 'clicked email' straight into CLICK (connectors/klaviyo/mapping.py:58-59), with no check of a bot property. ch_open_rate is a profile feature (profile/features.py), and opens are inflated by Apple Mail Privacy Protection. Overstated: scanners click every link in every message, so they add uniform noise across themes and do not make one theme look like a winner. LiftPerClick's dilution is a uniform rescale that keeps the ranking. Link-scanning gateways are mostly corporate, and the target is B2C (mostly Gmail and consumer addresses in India, plus WhatsApp, where there are no scanner clicks). The real harm is a minority of addresses with inflated personal factors getting extra cheap emails. Worth fixing, but minor for this market.
